description: Buoyancy Breakers explores flame behaviour in microgravity to improve spacecraft fire safety. I have a background in aerospace engineering, CFD, combustion, propulsion, and thermal analysis. We are looking for teammates skilled in Python, machine learning, data analysis, and web development to build an interactive dashboard and extract meaningful insights from NASA's combustion data. Curiosity and willingness to learn are welcome!
summary:
FireGuard is an interactive fire-safety research dashboard developed to explore how fire behaves in microgravity and what this means for the safety of future space missions.

On Earth, gravity plays an important role in flame movement, heat transfer and the transport of gases. In microgravity, these processes behave differently, creating challenges for fire detection, prevention and suppression in spacecraft and space habitats.

To address this challenge, we brought together selected NASA combustion investigations into a single platform where users can explore research findings, compare investigations and identify which studies are most relevant to different mission environments. The dashboard supports six scenarios, including lunar habitats, Mars habitats, pressurized rovers and orbital stations.

Our goal is to make NASA combustion research easier to understand and use, helping engineers and researchers identify important fire-safety considerations for future human space exploration.
details:
Project Details – FireGuard: Fire-Safety Evidence Engine

1. What does FireGuard do?

FireGuard is an interactive research dashboard designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore, compare and interpret for future human space missions.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity because buoyancy-driven convection is significantly reduced. This affects flame shape, heat transfer, transport of combustion products, smoke formation and flame propagation. Understanding these differences is important when designing fire prevention, detection and suppression systems for spacecraft and planetary habitats.

2. How does it work?

The dashboard brings together 12 curated groups of NASA combustion investigations, including BASS, FLEX, SAME, ACME, Saffire, DAFT and other research programmes.

Users can:

  • Explore and search combustion investigations.
  • Filter research based on topics and fuel categories.
  • Rank investigations using six weighted relevance criteria.
  • Compare up to four investigations at a time.
  • Examine research relevance across six mission scenarios: lunar bases, Mars habitats, pressurized rovers, spacesuits, orbital stations and Earth applications.
  • Explore engineering considerations and research gaps relevant to future space exploration.

The ranking system uses team-defined relevance scores to help users prioritize research. These scores are not experimental measurements or validated fire-risk predictions.

3. Engineering approach and creativity

The central idea behind FireGuard is to connect fundamental combustion research with practical spaceflight fire-safety questions.

Instead of presenting NASA investigations as isolated research studies, we organize them around mission environments and engineering requirements. This allows users to understand which research areas may be relevant to a particular exploration scenario and where further investigation is needed.

We also distinguish between experimental evidence, engineering interpretation and limitations when considering the transfer of microgravity research to lunar and Martian gravity environments.

4. Tools and technologies

The project was developed as a browser-based interactive dashboard using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The platform includes interactive filtering, comparison features, scenario-based ranking and a research exploration interface.

Additional technologies used in the development workflow include GitHub for source-code management, Netlify for web deployment and OpenAI API integration as a planned AI-assisted research explanation feature. The local evidence-search functionality provides an alternative when the AI service is unavailable.

5. Expected benefits and impact

FireGuard aims to reduce the effort required to navigate multiple combustion research investigations and make their relevance easier to understand.

It can serve as a starting point for aerospace engineers, researchers and students investigating spacecraft fire safety. By connecting combustion science with mission-specific considerations, the platform supports better research planning and helps identify areas where additional testing and validation are necessary.

Our long-term vision is to develop FireGuard into a more comprehensive evidence-support platform for fire-safety research in spacecraft, lunar habitats and future Mars missions.
